papers.title: A hardware-efficient variational ansatz with an exact diagonal metric for real- and imaginary-time evolution and Haar sampling
papers.summary: An n-qubit ansatz whose quantum geometric (Fubini–Study) metric is diagonal in closed form, so natural-gradient optimisation and variational time evolution need no costly metric measurements. Implemented in the QuantumSymmetry package.

papers.title: Comment on 'On computing quantum waves exactly from classical action'
papers.venue: Submitted to Proceedings of the Royal Society A
papers.summary: A Comment showing that the exact classical-action construction of Lohmiller and Slotine omits the amplitude-curvature (quantum-potential) term of the Madelung-Bohm decomposition, so it reduces to the WKB/Van Vleck approximation, exact only in special cases (plane waves, the Coulomb problem) but not in general.

papers.title: Symmetry-adapted qubit encoding with complete active space and Bravyi–Kitaev mapping for quantum chemistry on a quantum computer
papers.summary: Extends symmetry-adapted encodings with complete-active-space approximations and compatibility with the Bravyi–Kitaev mapping, enabling larger molecules on near-term hardware.

papers.title: Periodic symmetry-adapted encoding: qubit reduction in crystalline electronic structure
papers.summary: Extends symmetry-adapted encoding from molecules to periodic solids, using space-group symmetries to save qubits in crystalline electronic-structure simulations.

papers.title: Electron–molecule scattering via R-matrix variational algorithms on a quantum computer
papers.summary: The first quantum-computing formulation of the R-matrix method for electron–molecule collisions: variational circuits recover the spectral information encoding R-matrix boundary amplitudes, demonstrated on electron scattering from H₂.

papers.title: Pascal's pyramid and number projection operators for quantum computation
papers.summary: Explicit qubit operators that project onto fixed particle-number sectors under the Jordan–Wigner mapping, revealing a structure of generalised binomial coefficients visualised as a Pascal's pyramid.

papers.title: The open-source Python package QuantumSymmetry: the water molecule on four qubits
papers.summary: Presents QuantumSymmetry, which takes a molecular geometry and basis set and automatically constructs symmetry-adapted qubit operators, demonstrated by simulating the water molecule on just four qubits.

papers.title: Symmetry-adapted encodings for qubit number reduction by point-group and other Boolean symmetries
papers.summary: Introduces symmetry-adapted encodings, which exploit a molecule's point-group and other Boolean symmetries to map its electronic structure onto fewer qubits; the paper behind QuantumSymmetry.

papers.title: The Variational Quantum Eigensolver: a review of methods and best practices
papers.summary: A comprehensive review of the Variational Quantum Eigensolver, the leading near-term quantum algorithm for ground-state energies in chemistry and materials, covering its components, error sources and best practices.

thesis.title: Qubits, Symmetry and Geometry: Quantum Algorithms for Molecular Physics
